steps.title: Make 10× aCSF stock
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of 10× artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF) stock in ddH₂O without NaHCO₃ by adding: NaCl 126 mM (73.63 g), KCl 2.5 mM (1.86 g), NaH₂PO₄·H₂O 1.25 mM (1.724 g), CaCl₂·2H₂O 2.0 mM (2.94 g), MgSO₄ anhydrous 2.0 mM (2.408 g), Dextrose 10 mM (18.02 g). Store the stock at 4 °C; for the final working solution dilute 1:10 in ddH₂O and add 2.18 g NaHCO₃.

steps.title: Make 10× sucrose aCSF stock
steps.instruction: Prepare 500 mL of 10× modified aCSF (sucrose) stock in ddH₂O without NaHCO₃ by adding: Sucrose 36 g (210 mM final after dilution), KCl 2.5 mM (0.932 g), NaH₂PO₄·H₂O 1.25 mM (0.862 g), CaCl₂·2H₂O 0.5 mM (0.37 g), MgSO₄ anhydrous 10 mM (6.02 g), Dextrose 10 mM (9.01 g), Ascorbic acid 0.4 mM (0.35 g), KCH₃SO₃ 135.5 mM (1.637 g). Store at 4 °C; for the final working solution dilute 1:10 in ddH₂O, add 1.09 g NaHCO₃, and retain the 36 g sucrose in the final solution.

steps.title: Prepare K internal solution
steps.instruction: Mix all ingredients except ATP and GTP in ~75 mL ice‑cold ddH₂O (on ice). Add KCH₃SO₃ 135.5 mM (1.637 g), EGTA 0.2 mM (6.8 mg), KCl 5 mM (33.5 mg), NaCl 2.5 mM (13.15 mg), Na₂‑phosphocreatine 5 mM (114.8 mg), HEPES 10 mM (238.3 mg). Titrate pH to 7.3–7.4 with 1 N KOH using 50 µL increments, then bring volume to 90 mL with ice‑cold ddH₂O. Measure osmolarity (280–300 mOsm/kg). If acceptable, add ATP magnesium salt 2 mM (100 mg) and GTP sodium salt 0.21 mM (10 mg), readjust pH with 1 N KOH, aliquot 1 mL into Eppendorf tubes and freeze at –20 °C. Perform all steps on ice.

steps.title: Dilute sucrose stock and oxygenate
steps.instruction: Dilute the 10× sucrose stock to a final volume of 500 mL, add the required NaHCO₃ (see stock note) and sucrose, stir with a magnetic stirrer, and verify osmolarity (290–310 mOsm). Oxygenate the solution for at least 15 min with carbogen. Freeze 120 mL of the solution in a 250 mL plastic cup at –20 °C for use on the experiment day; refrigerate the remaining sucrose and aCSF solutions.

steps.title: Dilute aCSF stock and oxygenate
steps.instruction: On the day of dissection, thaw the frozen sucrose cup by submerging it in warm tap water (prevent any water mixing). While it thaws, dilute the 10× aCSF stock to 500 mL, add NaHCO₃, and mix manually. Check osmolarity (290–310 mOsm). Pour enough of this aCSF into the slice chamber to fully submerge slices, insert a carbogen tube, and ensure no air bubbles are present. Do not move the chamber thereafter to avoid bubble formation.

steps.title: Set up ice containers and tools
steps.instruction: Fill two large containers with ice. In container 1, secure a Styrofoam perfusion board tilted downwards and place all surgical tools on the ice so that any part contacting the mouse brain stays chilled. In container 2, place a single‑edge industrial blade, the vibratome plate, and a dental‑wax sheet; set the vibratome plate on Kimwipes to prevent ice adhesion.

steps.title: Prepare anesthesia cocktail and inject mouse
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mL ketamine (1 g/10 mL) with 0.5 mL xylazine (20 mg/mL) in 8.5 mL injectable 0.9 % saline (total 10 mL). Inject intraperitoneally 20 µL per gram body weight (e.g., ≥0.4 mL for a 20 g mouse), delivering a dose of ~200 µg/g ketamine and 20 µg/g xylazine (terminal dosage). Keep the syringe needle pointing away, do not recap, and lay the syringe safely.

steps.title: Thaw frozen sucrose and prime syringe
steps.instruction: Submerge the frozen sucrose cup in warm tap water (no water contact). After a thin liquid layer forms, insert a carbogen tube into the mixture. Fill a 20 mL Luer‑lock syringe with the liquid sucrose, release any air bubbles, connect it to a scalp‑vein set, and dispense a small amount of sucrose to confirm the connection and remove excess bubbles. Submerge the syringe (still attached to the scalp‑vein set) completely in the ice of container 1.

steps.title: Crush frozen sucrose to slush
steps.instruction: Flip the frozen sucrose block so the thawed side faces upward. Using the flat end of a microspatula, crush the block until it reaches a slushy consistency; finish with a hand blender to eliminate remaining frozen pieces. Transfer 40 mL of the slushy sucrose into a 50 mL glass cup. Submerge both cups in container 2 ice and insert carbogen tubes into each cup to maintain oxygenation.

steps.title: Perfuse mouse brain with sucrose
steps.instruction: After the mouse is anesthetized, make a transverse skin incision, lift the skin with Bracken forceps, and cut across the raised skin with sharp‑blunt dissecting scissors. Insert the scissors into the opening, cut through both sides of the rib cage, then cut the diaphragm. Expose the thoracic cavity, cut the right atrium with fine spring scissors, and insert the scalp‑vein set needle (connected to the sucrose syringe) into the left ventricle apex. Slowly inject sucrose to perfuse the brain.

steps.title: Detach mouse head and finalize dissection
steps.instruction: Suspend the mouse by its ears, make a transverse incision under the head, and proceed with brain extraction (standard rodent brain dissection). Keep all tools and the brain immersed in the oxygenated sucrose solution until slicing.

steps.title: Patch cell and form gigaseal
steps.instruction: Place the brain slice in the recording chamber, bring a borosilicate glass pipette (filament, fire‑polished, 10 cm length, OD 1.5 mm, ID 0.86 mm) to a target neuron, and approach to obtain a ≥1 GΩ seal. Adjust the holding voltage to the expected resting potential (≈ –60 mV for pacemaker neurons). Perform capacitance compensation in the MultiClamp 700B (auto Cp fast and Cp slow, fine‑tune Cp slow manually). Apply a slight negative pressure to break into the cell and achieve whole‑cell configuration. Verify low access resistance (≈ 300 pA) and action‑potential overshoot of at least –20 mV (preferably 0 mV).

steps.title: Configure proximal illumination
steps.instruction: With the high‑magnification water‑immersion objective in place, slide the IRDIC analyzer fitted with a disk containing a central pinhole into the analyzer slot just behind the objective. Close the diaphragm of the incident‑light pathway to restrict illumination to the proximal region.

steps.title: Record brief blue‑light pulses
steps.instruction: In voltage‑clamp mode, hold the cell at a hyperpolarized potential (e.g., –70 mV) and deliver a 1‑ms 470 nm blue‑light pulse. Repeat several times and average the responses. Include synaptic blockers in the aCSF: DNQX 10 mM, D‑AP5 50 mM, gabazine 10 mM, and CGP55845 2 mM. Adjust the LED driver voltage so that the evoked inward current is ≈ 10 pA (proximal illumination typically requires a larger LED voltage than full‑field).

steps.title: Switch to full‑field illumination
steps.instruction: Open the incident‑light diaphragm, remove the IRDIC analyzer with its disk, pull the high‑mag water‑immersion objective out, and insert the low‑magnification air/dry objective to achieve full‑field illumination of the dendritic arbor.

steps.title: Program sinusoidal LED perturbations
steps.instruction: Using Signal 6 (or equivalent), create a concatenated sinusoidal waveform composed of the following frequencies and durations (in parentheses): 0.2 Hz (5 s), 0.4 Hz (5 s), 0.6 Hz (5 s), 0.8 Hz (5 s), 1 Hz (5 s), 1.2 Hz (5 s), 1.4 Hz (5 s), 1.6 Hz (5 s), 1.8 Hz (5 s), 2 Hz (3 s), 3 Hz (3 s), 4 Hz (3 s), 5 Hz (3 s), 6 Hz (3 s), 8 Hz (3 s), 10 Hz (3 s), 12 Hz (3 s), 14 Hz (3 s), 16 Hz (3 s), 18 Hz (3 s), 20 Hz (3 s). Set the LED driver amplitude (by trial‑and‑error) to generate currents of a few tens of picoamperes. Use a sampling frequency of 10 kHz. Optionally repeat the protocol to average responses or invert the waveform for history‑dependence studies.

steps.title: Run Poisson barrage stimulation
steps.instruction: Program 25 realizations of a Poisson barrage of brief (0.5–1 ms) 470 nm pulses with exponentially distributed inter‑pulse intervals (mean IPI chosen based on the neuron’s spontaneous firing rate). Generate the waveforms in MATLAB (or similar) and upload to Signal 6. Set pulse intensity to affect spike timing without markedly changing the overall firing rate (intensity differs for proximal vs. full‑field). After establishing perforated‑patch configuration (allow perforation to advance in voltage‑ or current‑clamp), record spiking during each barrage while synaptic blockers (DNQX, D‑AP5, gabazine, CGP55845) remain present.

steps.title: Test oscillatory entrainment
steps.instruction: Following gigaseal formation and perforation advancement, estimate the neuron’s autonomous firing rate. Program on‑the‑fly 30–60 s sinusoidal LED protocols at frequencies below, above, and near the autonomous rate (including integer multiples). Run each protocol, adjusting LED intensity to produce a slight perturbation. Analyze spike timing relative to the sinusoid to compute phase locking and circular‑variance vectors as described in the manuscript.
